jobs.description:
Advisors · RIAs · Portfolio Workflows

About the job

PortfolioFuture is an independent fund discovery and intelligence company. We use empirical research to discover, evaluate, and rank ETFs and mutual funds, and identify where they can credibly compete for allocations in portfolios.

Our research connects more than 10,000 funds with institutional investors, 23,000+ advisory firms, and 400,000+ financial advisors, supporting fund discovery, portfolio analytics, and asset-manager distribution intelligence.

As a Wealth Research Analyst, you will study how financial advisors and wealth managers evaluate the funds PortfolioFuture identifies. The role covers advisor research, portfolio workflows, fund consideration, and the development of market intelligence used across PortfolioFuture.

You will speak with advisors, RIAs, and wealth-management professionals to understand what makes a fund worth investigating, what keeps it out of a portfolio, and how those judgments differ across firms and client types.

What you’ll work on

• Speak with financial advisors, RIAs, and wealth-management professionals about funds identified through PortfolioFuture’s research.
• Study how advisors compare competing ETFs and mutual funds and what makes a fund worth further consideration.
• Document the recurring questions, objections, and concerns that come up around specific funds and investment strategies.
• Research how advisors judge a fund’s strategy, positioning, fees, track record, and role in a portfolio.
• Compare how different advisors evaluate the same investment product.
• Turn qualitative conversations into structured market intelligence the rest of PortfolioFuture can act on.
• Identify gaps between how a fund manager describes a strategy and how the wealth-management market understands it.
• Study how a fund enters an advisor’s consideration set and what moves it from awareness to real due diligence.
• Work with PortfolioFuture’s substitution and decomposition research so advisor conversations stay grounded in evidence.
• Use large language models and other tools to organize, summarize, and analyze qualitative research at scale.
• Share what you learn with research, product, and distribution teams so findings reach the people who can use them.
• Test whether the patterns you observe hold across firm size, client type, and market environment.

What we’re looking for

• Background in finance, economics, business, wealth management, communications, or a related field.
• Strong interest in financial advisors, RIAs, wealth management, ETFs, and mutual funds.
• Ability to conduct thoughtful professional conversations and ask useful follow-up questions.
• Ability to understand an investment product well enough to discuss it with experienced advisors.
• Strong listening skills and the ability to identify patterns across many different conversations.
• Ability to turn qualitative feedback into clear, structured written findings.
• Comfort reaching out to and speaking with experienced wealth-management professionals.
• Ability to communicate what you learned clearly, including what you are not yet sure about.
• Experience in wealth management, financial advisory, investment product distribution, or practice management is useful but not required.
• Experience with research interviews, qualitative analysis, CRM data, or survey design is a plus.

PortfolioFuture research

Fund Substitution identifies ETFs and mutual funds that can serve similar portfolio roles, using return similarity, relative performance, tracking error, and fees.

Fund Decomposition separates returns explained by investable market exposures from residual performance, evaluating replication quality, residual alpha, and risk.

Fund Opportunity ranks ETFs and mutual funds across four dimensions: Similar Fund Ranking, Addressable Market, Pure Alpha, and Diversification Benefits.

PortfolioFuture’s research is independent. Commercial relationships do not affect which funds are surfaced, how they rank, or the conclusions reached.

jobs.title: Junior Compliance Analyst
jobs.description:
About Pockyt

Pockyt is building the AI-native infrastructure for global money movement. We give merchants a single platform to accept payments from anywhere, send money globally, and manage funds through Global Virtual Accounts and stablecoins — but our ambition runs deeper than the rails themselves. We're architecting the connective tissue that lets capital move across borders the way information moves across the internet: instantly, intelligently, and autonomously.
We serve a wide spectrum of merchants, from sophisticated enterprise platforms running complex multi-currency operations to the next generation of AI-powered startups, including the one-person unicorns we believe are about to reshape the global economy. Today, that means one integration, one account view, and one place to track everything. Tomorrow, it means a financial layer that AI agents can natively transact on — where money flows are orchestrated, optimized, and reconciled without human bottlenecks.

Our mission is to make global commerce frictionless. We're not building another payments platform. We're building the operating system for how value moves in an agentic, borderless economy.

The Role

We're hiring a Junior Compliance Analyst to keep the engine of our compliance function running. You'll own the high-volume, detail-heavy work that every good compliance program depends on across both our cross-border payments and merchant acquiring programs: chasing documents, checking files for completeness, clearing first-level screening hits, prepping evidence packages, and keeping case records clean and audit-ready. When something needs a judgment call, you'll assemble the facts and escalate it to the Compliance Manager or CCO with a clear summary — and you'll learn how those calls get made.

This is a great fit for someone early in their compliance career who is meticulous, likes a well-organized queue, and wants a fast, hands-on education in BSA/AML and merchant acquiring compliance at a cross-border payments company. Because we're actively automating our workflows with our Product Engineering team, you'll also be the person who knows exactly where the repetitive work lives — and your notes on it will shape what gets automated next.

What You'll Do

Onboarding file prep:
Collect and chase merchant KYB/KYC documents, check applications for completeness, verify basic entity and UBO details against registries, and flag gaps before a file goes to review
Merchant acquiring support:
Help underwrite new card-acquiring merchants by verifying business model and MCC, reviewing merchant websites for prohibited or restricted products and required policies (refunds, terms, privacy), and checking principals against MATCH and internal decline lists; escalate anything outside our risk appetite with a clear summary
First-level screening:
Run and clear obvious false-positive sanctions, PEP, and adverse media hits; document the rationale; escalate anything ambiguous with a clean summary
L1 transaction monitoring triage:
Work through ThetaRay alerts (in transition to a new tool), close out clear-cut false positives per the playbook, and route the rest up with the relevant transaction history pulled together
Acquiring risk monitoring:
Track merchant chargeback and fraud ratios against card network thresholds, flag merchants trending toward program limits, and pull the transaction and dispute data the Compliance Manager needs to decide next steps
RFI coordination:
Draft and send routine RFIs to merchants, track responses and deadlines, follow up on overdue items, and log what comes back
Periodic review support:
Pull refreshed documents, re-run screening, and assemble the review file so the Compliance Manager can make the call
Evidence and record-keeping:
Maintain case logs, organize evidence packages in SharePoint, and keep trackers accurate so any file can be handed to a banking partner or examiner on short notice
Data pulls and reporting:
Pull alert, case, onboarding, and chargeback metrics for weekly reviews, quarterly QA, and banking- and acquiring-partner requests
Process notes:
Keep a running list of repetitive steps and friction points, and help test AI-assisted and automated versions of your workflows once they ship

What We're Looking For

0–2 years in compliance, risk, KYC/onboarding, fraud operations, or a related role at a fintech, MSB, bank, or payments company — or a relevant internship plus strong interest in financial crimes
Exceptional attention to detail — you notice the mismatched date of birth, the expired document, and the missing page
Comfort with high-volume, repetitive work and the discipline to do it accurately every time
Strong organization — you can manage a queue, track deadlines, and keep a clean paper trail without being reminded
Good judgment about when to escalate, and the ability to summarize a case clearly and briefly
Clear, professional written communication with merchants and internal teams
AI fluency, or eagerness to build it — you're comfortable using Claude (or similar) for document review, summarization, and drafting
Curiosity about cross-border payments, stablecoins, and how compliance works in practice

Bonus Points

CAMS (or working toward it), ACAMS membership, or comparable training
Exposure to sanctions screening or transaction monitoring tools (ThetaRay, Hummingbird, Unit21, ComplyAdvantage, or similar)
Experience with KYB document review for business entities, especially cross-border or multi-entity structures
Exposure to merchant underwriting, card acquiring, or payment facilitator (PayFac) onboarding, including familiarity with Visa/Mastercard network rules, MCCs, MATCH, or chargeback/fraud monitoring programs such as Visa VAMP or Mastercard ECM/EFM
Mandarin, Spanish, or Portuguese language skills (helpful for LATAM/APAC merchant documents)
Strong spreadsheet skills for tracking and data pulls

How You'll Work

Rhythm:
Work the daily queue → clear or escalate → document → keep trackers current; weekly case reviews with the team and CCO; regular check-ins with the Compliance Manager on escalations
Collaboration:
Daily with onboarding and the Compliance Manager; regular contact with merchants on RFIs and document requests; occasional handoffs to product engineering on workflow fixes
Quality bar:
Every file you touch is complete and organized; every cleared hit has a documented rationale; every escalation arrives with the facts already pulled together

Success looks like:

About the job

PortfolioFuture is an independent fund discovery and intelligence company. We use empirical research to discover, evaluate, and rank ETFs and mutual funds, and identify where they can credibly compete for allocations in portfolios.

You will speak with advisors, RIAs, and wealth-management professionals to understand what makes a fund worth investigating, what keeps it out of a portfolio, and how those judgments differ across firms and client types.

What you’ll work on

• Speak with financial advisors, RIAs, and wealth-management professionals about funds identified through PortfolioFuture’s research.

• Research how advisors judge a fund’s strategy, positioning, fees, track record, and role in a portfolio.
• Compare how different advisors evaluate the same investment product.
• Turn qualitative conversations into structured market intelligence the rest of PortfolioFuture can act on.
• Identify gaps between how a fund manager describes a strategy and how the wealth-management market understands it.
• Study how a fund enters an advisor’s consideration set and what moves it from awareness to real due diligence.
• Work with PortfolioFuture’s substitution and decomposition research so advisor conversations stay grounded in evidence.
• Use large language models and other tools to organize, summarize, and analyze qualitative research at scale.
• Share what you learn with research, product, and distribution teams so findings reach the people who can use them.
• Test whether the patterns you observe hold across firm size, client type, and market environment.

What we’re looking for

• Background in finance, economics, business, wealth management, communications, or a related field.
• Strong interest in financial advisors, RIAs, wealth management, ETFs, and mutual funds.
• Ability to conduct thoughtful professional conversations and ask useful follow-up questions.

Keep a running list of repetitive steps and friction points, and help test AI-assisted and automated versions of your workflows once they ship

Work the daily queue → clear or escalate → document → keep trackers current; weekly case reviews with the team and CCO; regular check-ins with the Compliance Manager on escalations
Collaboration:
Daily with onboarding and the Compliance Manager; regular contact with merchants on RFIs and document requests; occasional handoffs to product engineering on workflow fixes

Every file you touch is complete and organized; every cleared hit has a documented rationale; every escalation arrives with the facts already pulled together

a queue that stays current, onboarding files that reach review complete the first time, clean and consistent case records, fast RFI turnaround, early flags on merchants trending toward chargeback limits, and a growing ability to handle more of the decision-making yourself.

Learn compliance from the ground up at a fast-moving, AI-native fintech, working directly alongside the CCO and Compliance Manager

A leading global alternative investment manager headquartered in New York City is seeking a Security Master Business Analyst (Consultant) to join its Data Services team as a key contributor to a firm-wide security master implementation project.

This is a hands-on role for someone who thrives in a fast-paced, detail-driven data environment. Responsibilities:

Serve as a key business analyst on the firm's security master implementation, gathering and documenting business and functional requirements from stakeholders across Data Services, Technology, and Operations
Perform deep, hands-on data analysis using SQL and Excel to profile, reconcile, and validate securities reference data across source systems and the target security master platform

5+ years of experience as a business analyst, data analyst, or similar role within a financial services organization (asset management, private equity, hedge fund, or investment bank preferred)

Experience with security master platforms (e.g., GoldenSource, Bloomberg AIM/DL, Eagle STAR/PACE, SimCorp, Charles River, Markit EDM, or similar)

Employment Logistics

The Data Analytics Senior Specialist designs, develops, and maintains clear, reliable reporting and analytics solutions that help business teams understand performance, identify key drivers, and make informed decisions. This role builds and improves dashboards, recurring reports, and ad hoc analyses that translate data into meaningful business stories. The position partners with cross-functional teams to turn business questions and operational goals into clearly defined metrics, trends, and user-friendly visualizations.

Two (2) weeks paid pregnancy disability leave, four (4) weeks paid parental bonding leave
Additional wellness and employee assistance programs

5+ years of relevant experience with a Bachelor’s degree or equivalent
Deep understanding of industry principles and operational event data concepts
In-depth knowledge of standard office software and data analytics technologies, including Power BI dashboards and SQL
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Experience translating analytical results into clear, actionable deliverables

KPIs, metrics & data visualization: Translate operational goals, business questions, and reporting needs into actionable KPIs, clearly defined metrics, trends, and easy-to-use visuals that support decision-making.
Data visibility & process improvement: Partner with business teams to identify, scope, and address gaps in data visibility, including missing fields, unclear definitions, and inconsistent processes, with guidance from senior Analytics or Engineering partners.
Reporting quality & metric governance: Improve reporting consistency and quality by following documentation standards and applying shared definitions and metric-governance frameworks.
Ad hoc analysis & business insights: Provide ad hoc analyses that support strategic initiatives, operational improvements, leadership inquiries, and broader business decision-making.

Paving Your Way To Your Success

You collaborate effectively within a team environment to translate business needs into useful analytics solutions.
You thrive in a fast-paced environment, prioritizing tasks and maintaining accuracy while managing multiple requests and changing priorities.
You maintain professionalism in your communication and interactions with business and technical partners.
You develop solutions using limited information or precedent, adapting existing methods as needed.
You analyze unusual situations using advanced analytical and problem-solving techniques to identify root causes.
